description: Aquarius zodiac sign: personality traits, strengths and challenges, love, career, decans and dates (January 20 to February 18).
answer: In Western astrology, Aquarius is the eleventh sign of the zodiac, a fixed air sign ruled by Uranus. It is traditionally associated with originality, independence, idealism and community-minded thinking. The Sun is in Aquarius from about January 20 to February 18. The exact dates shift by a day from year to year.

sections.heading: Aquarius personality traits
paragraphs: Aquarius is the water bearer, a figure pouring water from a jar onto the earth below. The name confuses people, because Aquarius is not a water sign at all; the water stands for knowledge, ideas and fresh perspectives poured out for everyone to share. That generosity of mind is central to the sign. Aquarians are often described as inventive, unconventional and quietly stubborn, people who care about humanity in general and fairness in particular. They tend to be friendly with almost everyone while holding something of themselves back, as if observing the human experiment with interest from slightly outside it.

Aquarius is a fixed air sign ruled by Uranus, with Saturn, its traditional ruler, adding structure in the background. Air signs think, talk and connect, and fixed signs hold their position, so Aquarius often has strong, carefully reasoned convictions it will not easily give up. Uranus, discovered in the age of revolutions, is associated with sudden change, technology, rebellion and originality. Saturn contributes a sober streak and an interest in systems. The blend explains the sign's reputation as a reformer: forward-looking and sometimes radical in its ideas, yet often surprisingly methodical about how to put them into practice.

sections.heading: Aquarius strengths and challenges
paragraphs: Aquarius often sees what could be different before anyone else does. It is an original thinker, comfortable challenging received wisdom and good at spotting patterns across systems. It tends to treat people as equals regardless of status, which makes it a fair-minded friend and colleague. Aquarians are usually loyal to causes and communities, generous with their ideas and willing to stand apart from the crowd when principle requires it. They can be fascinating company, curious about everything from science to subcultures, and their friendships often last for decades without demanding constant upkeep.

Aquarian detachment can be hard to live with. In emotional moments it may retreat into analysis, offering a theory when someone wanted a hug, and it can seem aloof or impersonal. The fixed quality means opinions are held firmly, sometimes to the point of contrarian stubbornness, arguing the opposite simply because everyone else agrees. Love for humanity in the abstract can sit oddly beside impatience with the specific humans nearby. Some Aquarians also guard their independence so carefully that closeness feels like a threat, and they may present unpredictability as a principle when it is really avoidance.

sections.heading: Aquarius in love and relationships
paragraphs: Aquarius usually wants a partner who is a friend first. It is drawn to minds it finds interesting and often bonds through conversation, shared causes or unusual interests long before anything romantic is said. In love it offers loyalty, acceptance and a refreshing lack of possessiveness; it is unlikely to try to change you and will probably encourage you to be more fully yourself. It typically needs space, intellectual stimulation and a relationship that respects both people's independence. Conventional scripts about how love should look can feel stifling to it.

The friction often lies in emotional expression. Partners may feel that Aquarius is more comfortable discussing feelings than having them, or that it keeps a part of itself permanently out of reach. Sudden withdrawals for alone time can be misread as rejection. What helps is directness without drama: telling Aquarius clearly what you need, and not taking its need for distance personally. Aquarius can help by explaining its silences before they become mysterious, and by practising staying present with a partner's feelings rather than solving or analysing them straight away.

sections.heading: Aquarius at work
paragraphs: Aquarius tends to flourish where innovation is welcome and hierarchy is light. It brings original ideas, technical curiosity and an interest in improving how things work for everyone, which suits technology, science, engineering, research, social enterprise, activism, policy, product design and any role involving networks or communities. As a leader it is usually egalitarian and visionary, preferring to set a direction and let capable people get on with it. It is often the one who questions a rule that everyone else had stopped noticing, and then proposes a cleaner way to do it.

Pitfalls include impatience with tradition, resistance to authority even when it is reasonable, and a habit of drifting from a project once the intellectual puzzle is solved. Aquarius may also underestimate the emotional side of change, pushing a good idea without bringing people along. With money it can be idiosyncratic: indifferent to status spending yet happy to invest in a new gadget, cause or experimental scheme. Pairing vision with a patient implementer, explaining the human reasons behind proposals, and keeping a steady savings habit all help.

sections.heading: Growth and the three Aquarius decans
paragraphs: Aquarius tends to grow by bringing its ideals closer to home. Caring about the world is admirable; caring for the particular people in your life, with their irrational moods and ordinary needs, is where those ideals are tested. Try noticing when you move into analysis during an emotional conversation, and simply stay with the feeling for a few minutes longer. Let a friend help you instead of always being the self-sufficient one. Ask whether a firmly held opinion is still serving you or whether it has become part of your identity. Independence and closeness are not opposites. Keep the originality and the conscience, and let warmth be as visible as your intelligence.

Aquarius divides into three decans of ten degrees each. The first, roughly January 20 to January 29, belongs to Uranus; the second, about January 30 to February 8, to Mercury; and the third, around February 9 to February 18, to Venus. Each has its own page, and every Aquarius birthday links to its decan.

faq.question: Is Aquarius a water sign?
faq.answer: No. Despite the water bearer symbol, Aquarius is an air sign. The water in its jar is usually read as knowledge and ideas shared with everyone. Like the other air signs, Gemini and Libra, Aquarius is associated with thought, communication and connection.

faq.question: Who is Aquarius most compatible with?
faq.answer: Aquarius is often described as getting on well with fellow air signs Gemini and Libra, who enjoy its ideas and independence. Fire signs Aries and Sagittarius bring energy and a shared appetite for freedom. Leo, its opposite sign, adds warmth and attraction. The whole birth chart gives a more complete view.

faq.question: What are the dates for Aquarius?
faq.answer: About January 20 to February 18. The Sun's entry into each sign moves by a day or so between years, so birthdays at either end are cusp dates; the zodiac sign calculator settles them for a specific year.

faq.question: What are the three Aquarius decans?
faq.answer: The first decan (0° to 9°) is linked with Uranus, the second (10° to 19°) with Mercury and the third (20° to 29°) with Venus, following the rulers of the air signs in zodiac order.
